# Explain Cache Conflicts and Related Memory-Access Problems

[← AMD](../README.md) · [Every AMD question](../../amd.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/explain-cache-conflicts-and-related-memory-access-problems)

---

Describe a cache-line conflict with a concrete address example, and then contrast it with false sharing and GPU shared-memory bank conflicts.

### Constraints & Assumptions
The term "cache-line conflict" appears without a specific hardware context. Start by clarifying which mechanism is meant. For a concrete cache-set illustration, suppose a set-associative cache with line size L bytes, S sets, and A ways, using the set index `floor(address/L) mod S`.

### Clarifying Questions
Is the issue cache-set eviction, coherence traffic between CPU cores, or serialization of scratchpad banks on a GPU? What is the access pattern, alignment, and hardware mapping?

### What a Strong Answer Covers
A specific mapping from addresses to lines or sets, the resulting contention, and fixes suited to the actual mechanism.

### Follow-up Questions
How can a working set that fits in total cache capacity still thrash? Why does padding help? When would padding only increase memory usage without resolving the bottleneck?

Overview:
Describe cache-set conflicts via address mapping, then separate eviction from false sharing and GPU bank conflicts so that padding and layout changes address the correct cause.
